name: SentinelOne: pull threats
description: Every 5 minutes, fetch SentinelOne threats created since the previous run (Management API v2.1) and ingest each one as a pending alert (source sentinelone, deduplicated on the threat id).

params.label: SentinelOne console host
params.help: Your management console host name, as in the browser address bar. Host only, no https://.

secrets.name: S1_API_TOKEN
secrets.description: API token of a SentinelOne service user.

setup:
## SentinelOne side
1. **Settings > Users > Service Users > Create New Service User**, scope **Account** (or the Site you want to pull), role **Viewer** for pulling only; use a role that can disconnect agents (e.g. **IR Team** or **SOC**) if the same token will also run *SentinelOne: disconnect agent*.
2. Set an expiry date and copy the API token into the secret `S1_API_TOKEN`, allowed for your console host. Renew it before it expires (runs fail with HTTP 401 until you do; the missed window is re-read, up to 24 h back).
3. Set `S1_CONSOLE` to the console host.

## How it works
- `pull`: `GET /web/api/v2.1/threats?createdAt__gt=<since>&limit=100` with header `Authorization: ApiToken <token>`. `<since>` is the fire time of the last successful run.
- A non-200 answer (401 expired token, 403, 429 throttled) ends the run as failed (`SentinelOne pull failed: ... HTTP <status>`); the next run re-reads the window.
- One alert per item of `data`: external id = threat `id`; title = `threatInfo.threatName` + `agentRealtimeInfo.agentComputerName`; severity from `threatInfo.confidenceLevel`: malicious + classification Ransomware = critical, malicious = high, suspicious = medium, anything else = low. Payload = the full threat.
- Overlapping windows are safe: a threat already ingested is not created twice.

## Limits
- One page per run: at most **100 threats per window**; the `pagination.nextCursor` of a full page is not followed, and the next successful run starts at this run's fire time. Raise `limit` (API max 1000) and `max_items` on `loop` (max 500) together if needed.
- After failed runs the window is re-read from the last successful run, at most 24 h back.
- Threats only; SentinelOne *alerts* (STAR / custom detection rules, `/web/api/v2.1/cloud-detection/alerts`) are not pulled.

To double-check in your console's API doc: the `createdAt__gt` filter and `limit` on `GET /threats`, and the `threatInfo` field names.

Docs relied on: the Management API reference is behind the console login (`https://<console>/api-doc/overview`, API v2.1). Public sources used: public open-source SentinelOne API clients (`/web/api/v2.1/` base, `Authorization: ApiToken <token>`, `threats?createdAt__gt=`, `agents/actions/disconnect` with `{"filter": {...}}`) and the PS-SentinelOne module (https://powershellgallery.com/packages/PS-SentinelOne). Double-check against your console's API doc before enabling.

config.message: SentinelOne pull failed: threats query returned HTTP {{ steps.pull.output.status }}

config.title: {{ (loop.item.get('threatInfo') or {}).get('threatName') or 'SentinelOne threat' }} on {{ (loop.item.get('agentRealtimeInfo') or {}).get('agentComputerName') or 'unknown host' }}
config.severity: {% set ti = loop.item.get('threatInfo') or {} %}{{ 'critical' if ti.get('confidenceLevel') == 'malicious' and ti.get('classification') == 'Ransomware' else 'high' if ti.get('confidenceLevel') == 'malicious' else 'medium' if ti.get('confidenceLevel') == 'suspicious' else 'low' }}
